audit.why: Chart is Warwick on all seven rows in both layers, matching packet.levelChart exactly and the 55.57% winrate over 700 games. No mirror audit exists yet, so nothing to reconcile.

Spike windows are already specific and non-generic: level 1-3, level 6 with his ultimate, first item, and late. His E is a flat 10s at every rank, which is what the 'ten seconds of nothing' framing correctly leans on, and his R is 120s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Windows kept; only the level-6 mechanics were wrong (see point 4).

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important interaction in this matchup is absent, and the page states its opposite: whys[4], spikes[1].text and the mid prose all say Infinite Duress 'suppresses him straight through' his ultimate and hard-counters it.
audit.why: His R carries the grounding flag — it shuts off enemy dashes. Both of your engage tools are dashes: Jaws of the Beast is a lunge and Infinite Duress is a leap. So his ultimate denies your engage rather than losing to it, and it also carries an execute threshold. The correct advice is to ult BEFORE the artifact lands.
audit.corrected: Restated across whys[4], spikes[1].text and mid: his R grounds, denying both Q and the R leap, so the ult goes first and you stay above the execute threshold.
sources: ownerKit Q and R dash flags

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8].t says 'Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.'
audit.why: His W is flagged as a heal in the kit: it damages him during the effect and then heals back a portion at the end. Grievous Wounds reduces healing regardless of whether the source is lifesteal or a delayed refund, so the item advice talks a user out of a real counter.
audit.corrected: Line rewritten to say anti-heal still bites the W refund.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flagged "Primal Howl's" in the late prose as a probable wrong ability name.
audit.why: False positive — Primal Howl is Warwick's own E, and the sentence correctly credits its damage reduction.

edits.before: Infinite Duress is the totem answer: suppress him through his R Purgatory window and the execute never fires - a landed R is almost always a kill.
edits.after: His R grounds - it shuts off dashes, so it denies your Q lunge and the Infinite Duress leap alike. Ult before the artifact lands, never into it.

edits.before: Infinite Duress hard-counters his execute at 6 - you suppress him through the totem window.
edits.after: At 6 his R grounds dashes, denying your Duress leap - ult before it lands.

edits.before: At 6 you hold the trump card over his whole gameplan: R Purgatory needs a stationary execute window and Infinite Duress suppresses him straight through it, so a landed leap is a kill he cannot answer. Force the all-in whenever your R is up; his only defense is never being close enough to leap on.
edits.after: At 6 the order decides it: his R grounds, shutting off dashes, so it denies both Jaws of the Beast and the Infinite Duress leap while threatening an execute. Ult before the artifact lands, not after, and keep your health above his floor - a landed 1.5s suppress is still a kill he cannot answer.

edits.before: Early HP and MR blunt the nail chip (his damage is AP). A stopwatch/Zhonya’s-class answer beats Purgatory outright: untargetable at the floor = execute denied. Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.
edits.after: Early HP and MR blunt the nail chip (his damage is AP). A stopwatch/Zhonya’s-class answer beats Purgatory outright: untargetable at the floor = execute denied. Anti-heal still bites — his W refunds part of that self-damage at the end.

notes: The packet has no ability-name table for Locke (enemyAbilities is null), so I could not verify the names the page uses — Ritual Nails, Soul Ignition, Ashen Pursuit, Purgatory. One mismatch is visible: the page calls his Q 'Ritual Nails' while Riot's own description says he throws 'Soul Nails'. I did not rename anything, because the page's name may be the ability while 'Soul Nails' is the projectile, and a wrong rename is worse than an unverified one. Also unverified: the page repeatedly states he is a '125-range' champion, which appears in phases[0].why, breakdown.early, breakdown.wave and report[4].t — no such range exists in his kit data (Q 950, W 250, E 425, R 1000), so either the number is invented or it is his basic-attack range, which the files do not carry.
